newsitem.title: INDONESIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Nov 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Nov 4.

text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Indonesian press on November 4. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy. Telephone: (6221) 384-6364. Fax: (6221) 344-8404.
Research and Technology Minister Jusuf Habibie refused to speculate over the weekend on whether he will stand for the post of vice-president in the 1998 presedential elections.

Abdurrahaman Wahid, leader of the 30-million strong Islamic Nahdlatul Ulama (NU), met President Suharto on Saturday. It was their first meeting since Wahid, who has often been critical of the government, was re-elected NU chairman in 1994.

A consortium of 38 national banks will provide 1.2 trillion rupiah in 30-year loans to private power generating firms in North Sumatera and North Sulawesi. The companies, PT Tenaga Listrik Sibolga and PT Tenaga Listrik Amurang, are both owned by businessman Ibrahimn Risjad.

Three Indonesian ministers have criticised Nobel Peace Prize laureate Bishop Belo for comments made in an interview with German magazine 'Der Spiegel'. Belo reportedly said that Indonesia treated the people of the East Timor like "scabby dogs".

Cigarette manufacturers PT Djarum and PT Norojono are rumoured to be interested in buying a large stake in state-owned Bank Nasional Indonesia (BNI) when it is floated on the Jakarta Stock Exchange later this month.
